input.pql: PREDICT COUNT(orders.*, 0, 30, days) > 0 FOR EACH users.user_id

view.name: view_metric_parameter_and_month
view.yaml:
version: 0.1
source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.orders"
parameters:
  - name: min_price
    data_type: DOUBLE
    default: 50
filter: source.price >= min_price
joins:
  - name: users
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.users"
    on: source.user_id = users.user_id
dimensions:
  - name: order_id
    expr: source.order_id
  - name: user_id
    expr: source.user_id
  - name: ts
    expr: DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', source.ts)
  - name: price
    expr: source.price
measures:
  - name: revenue
    expr: SUM(source.price)

why: A row filter on a parameter, read as its default (a ParameterNote, DB/metric_view.py:924-944, RE/view_conversion.py:148), and a month dimension named as the raw date it truncates, so the raw date is added under a name of its own and taken as the time column (a TimeColumnNote, RE/graph.py:274). The view is created in the test schema from the yaml, its sources named with the {catalog} and {schema} placeholders the capture writes (no private name), each part backtick-quoted since Databricks reads a catalog's hyphen only quoted; its joins' on keys are bare, as people write them, so PyYAML reads each as the key true (KO3-40), which the reference reads too (DB/metric_view.py:825-909, join_cfg.get(True))
